hypothesis: GC/1.3 pointer conversion nodes and separate resource-result live ranges affect register coalescing even when conversions emit no instructions. This differs from prior direct-formal and delayed-event-copy attempts.
findings: Reusing the event parameter as the later resource improved canonical score to 98.776596%.
An inline owner getter changed allocation and improved canonical score to 98.82979%.

Pointer identity helpers without a cast coalesced unchanged. Adding the explicit (void *)(u32) conversion to the event value moved the early registers to their retail assignments: event/current/maximum/owner/world = r30/r25/r26/r27/r28; state/holder = r29/r31.

The conversion also works directly in the target function without any helper, reaching 99.893616%. The remaining two operand mismatches were at function offsets 0x110 and 0x124: the resolved resource used r30 instead of r25.
Giving the raw resource and resolved resource distinct C locals fixes both remaining operands. The final source contains only fn_800BF0C0, no helpers or assembly, and no changed compiler flags.
source_changes: Explicit 32-bit event pointer roundtrip into event_object.
Separate resource and resolved pointer locals.
registration: Promote only game/game_fn_800BF0C0.c from NonMatching to Matching after both canonical and relocation-strict objdiff reach 100%. Existing split remains unchanged.
